concept.title: Unordered Lists
concept.abstract: This section covers Unordered Lists — items presented as a co-equal collection where position does not affect meaning — and seven scenarios: consecutive bullet items, two-level nested bullet lists, three-level nested bullet lists, a block image between bullet items, a paragraph between bullet items, a table inside a list item, and an admonition between bullet items. The converter maps each unordered list to <ul><li> in concept and reference topics, or <choices> in task topics, based on the heading classification and content context.

conbody.p: An unordered list presents a collection of co-equal items where position does not affect meaning. The unordered list is typically used for prerequisites, supported platforms, product features, available options, feature list, and even terms and definition.

For the reader, a bulleted list communicates that the items are parallel and independent — none depends on another, and the set is complete as presented. The reader does not need to track position or sequence, only membership in the set.

The list level is controlled by the Increase and Decrease Indent buttons, determines nesting depth: level 1 is the top level, level 2 is the first nested level, level 3 is the second, and so on. Sometimes they are also defined by the tab alignment.
conbody.note: The list level assigned by list controls is what drives the nesting structure in the DITA output.
conbody.p: In well-structured HTML, unordered lists are created using native <ul> and <li> elements. Nested unordered lists represent sub-groupings within a parent item, while introductory paragraphs, images, tables, and notes provide supporting information without altering the non-sequential relationship between items.
